'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian separatist forces in Donbas|Pro-Russian forces]] of the [[Luhansk People's Republic]] claim to have taken the key town of [[Toshkivka]], 25 km south of [[Sieverodonetsk]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-backed-separatists-report-control-village-south-key-ukraine-battle-2022-06-20/ (Reuters)]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] fire [[missile]]s at a [[Chornomornaftogaz]] drilling oil facility in the [[Black Sea]], off [[Crimea]], injuring three workers, with seven others missing. Russia launches missile strikes on [[Odesa]] in retaliation for the attack. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2022/06/20/ukraine-news-russia-war-conflict-latest-putin-british-army/ (''The Telegraph'')] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2022/06/20/ukraine-news-russia-war-conflict-latest-putin-british-army/ (''The Telegraph'' 2)]
***A second [[Americans|American]] volunteer fighter dies in [[Ukraine]], after triggering a [[landmine]]. [https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/stephen-zabielski-russia-ukraine-conflict-1371094/ (''Rolling Stone'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2022 Bankass massacres]]
***[[Islamist]] [[insurgent]]s kill 132 civilians over the weekend in a series of attacks on three villages in the [[Bankass Cercle]] of [[Mali]]'s [[Mopti Region]], including [[Segue, Mali|Segue]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-united-nations-al-qaida-mali-africa-295e86bbe9796f69109f01e530841f0b (AP)]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**A [[bazaar]] in [[Nangarhar Province]] is bombed, which the [[United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan]] says has killed and injured "scores of people." The ruling [[Taliban]] confirm that at least ten people have been injured but cannot yet confirm if anyone has been killed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/attack-afghan-market-kills-wounds-scores-un-2022-06-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Two [[Jesuit]] [[priest]]s are murdered by gunmen in a church in [[Cerocahui]], [[Chihuahua (state)|Chihuahua]]. [https://apnews.com/article/religion-mexico-caribbean-1cb750c9dec14480e9d8344e6bc08d0c (AP)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**Eleven [[Syrian Army|soldiers]] and two civilians are killed in an attack on a bus travelling from [[Raqqa]] to [[Homs]]. The [[Islamic State]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/syrian-state-media-say-attack-on-army-bus-kills-13-troops/2022/06/20/ac71ad46-f073-11ec-ac16-8fbf7194cd78_story.html (''Washington Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/least-13-killed-attack-bus-syrias-raqqa-state-media-2022-06-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Panic buying]] is reported in the Russian [[Enclave and exclave|exclave]] of [[Kaliningrad Oblast|Kaliningrad]] after [[Lithuania]] banned the transit of some goods through its territory by [[Rail transport|rail]]. [[Governor of Kaliningrad Oblast|Kaliningrad Governor]] [[Anton Alikhanov]] calls for calm, while Russia condemns the ban. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/06/20/panic-buying-in-kaliningrad-as-lithuania-bans-rail-cargo-from-russia-a78044 (''The Moscow Times'')]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Affairs Ministry]] demands that Lithuania "immediately reverse" new restrictions on shipments of Russian goods to Kaliningrad, saying that the restrictions were "unprecedented" and "illegal", while also suggesting that [[Moscow]] could "take actions to protect its national interests". [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-lithuania-kaliningrad-cutoff/31906501.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Minister of National Defence (Canada)|Canadian defense minister]] [[Anita Anand]] announces an increase in defense spending to [[Canadian dollar|$]]5 billion in order to upgrade continental defense. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/anand-norad-radar-continental-defence-1.6494658 (CBC)]
*It is announced that [[Cape Verde]] will allocate a budget of $85 million to combat the effects of the war in Ukraine, which has caused an increase in the prices of gasoline and food, as 9% of Cape Verdeans are currently facing a food crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/world/cape-verde-budgets-85-million-cushion-ukraine-war-fallout-2022-06-20/ (Reuters)] [https://www.todayonline.com/world/cape-verde-budgets-us85-million-cushion-ukraine-war-fallout-1929281 (''Today Online'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A helicopter crashes near [[Burton in Lonsdale|Burton]], [[North Yorkshire]], [[England]], killing two people onboard. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-york-north-yorkshire-61869042 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute]]
**Dutch climate and energy minister [[Rob Jetten]] announces that the [[Netherlands]] will remove all restrictions on the operation of [[coal-fired power station]]s until at least 2024, in response to Russia's refusal to export [[natural gas]] to the country. Operations were previously limited to less than a third of [[Energy in the Netherlands|the total production]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/sustainability/germany-aims-shut-coal-power-plants-2030-energy-crisis-fossil-fuels-2758656  (CNA)]
*[[Environment and Climate Change Canada|Canadian Environmental Minister]] [[Steven Guilbeault]] announces that [[Canada]] will ban the sale of [[disposable product|single-use]] [[plastic]]s by December 2023, and will ban the export of these plastics by the end of 2025, with the first regulations to come into effect in December. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/6/20/canada-announces-ban-on-single-use-plastics (Al Jazeera)]
*A study published in ''[[List of Nature Research journals#N|Nature Food]]'' finds that the impact of food transportation on [[climate change]] is three times greater than was previously believed, making up 6% of global carbon emissions. [https://www.nature.com/articles/s43016-022-00531-w (''Nature Food'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belgium–Democratic Republic of the Congo relations]]
**The [[Federal Government of Belgium|Belgian government]] repatriates [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] independence leader and former [[Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|prime minister]] [[Patrice Lumumba]]'s remains, consisting of a tooth, through an official ceremony attended by his family at the [[Egmont Palace]] in [[Brussels]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/tooth-patrice-lumumba-congo-independence-returned-familly-belgium-rcna33270 (NBC News)]
*[[Ukraine]] ratifies the [[Istanbul Convention]]. [https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2022/06/20/7141621/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Recognition of same-sex unions in Japan]]
**The [[Osaka]] District Court rules that [[Japan]]'s ban on [[same-sex marriage]] is not "unconstitutional" in a ruling on a lawsuit filed by two [[male couple]]s and one [[lesbian|female couple]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7787854/japan-court-upholds-same-sex-marriage-ban/?cs=14232 (''The Canberra Times'')]
*Violent protests occur across [[India]], including the burning of [[Rail transport in India|trains]] in [[Hyderabad]], in response to [[Agnipath Scheme|proposed recruitment reforms]] in the [[Indian Armed Forces|military]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/6/20/we-have-been-cheated-indias-youth-reject-new-army-jobs-scheme (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 French legislative election]]
**[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]]'s party [[La République En Marche!|Renaissance]] is confirmed to lose its majority in the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] after yesterday's second round of [[Legislative elections in France|legislative elections]]. Both the [[left-wing]] [[Political alliance|alliance]] [[NUPES]] and the [[right-wing politics in France|right-wing]] party [[National Rally]] achieve significant electoral gains, forcing the [[Government of France|government]] to seek compromises with other parties during the upcoming legislative period for the first time since the [[1988 French legislative election|1988 legislative election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/macron-faces-tough-battle-control-parliament-france-votes-2022-06-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Next Israeli legislative election]]
**Leading members of the [[thirty-sixth government of Israel]] [[Naftali Bennett]] and [[Yair Lapid]] agree to dissolve the [[Knesset]], triggering a fifth snap election in just over three years. Lapid will serve as acting [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] until the election is held. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/foreign-minister-lapid-become-israels-prime-minister-israel-radio-2022-06-20/ (Reuters)]
